questions.question_text: A dispenser contains $5$ hexagon tokens and $7$ oval tokens. What is $P(\text{hexagon})$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Used the other outcome count as the denominator instead of the total count.
Used the oval count as favourable instead of the hexagon count.

questions.question_text: A pointer can stop on $12$ equal marks. A wave symbol covers $8$ marks. What is $P(\text{wave})$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Used the four non-wave marks as favourable instead of the eight wave marks.
Divided favourable marks by non-favourable marks instead of total marks.

questions.question_text: Outcomes J, K and L have weights in the ratio $1:4:5$. What is $P(K)$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Used the largest single weight as the total instead of adding all ratio parts.
Compared K only with J instead of with the whole ratio.

questions.question_text: A selector has $P(R)=\frac{3}{8}$ and $P(S)=\frac{1}{4}$. Outcome T fills the rest. What is $P(T)$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Added the known probabilities and reported their total instead of the remainder.
Subtracted the numerators without first writing both fractions with a common denominator.

questions.question_text: A box contains $9$ arrows, $3$ crosses and $6$ dots. What is the probability of drawing a cross or dot, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Counted only the crosses and ignored the dot outcome in the event.
Used arrows plus crosses as favourable instead of crosses plus dots.

questions.question_text: Four outcomes have weights $3,3,6,8$. What is the probability of either outcome with weight $3$, as a fraction in simplest form?

options.why: Included only one of the two outcomes with weight three.
Compared the favourable total six only with the non-favourable total fourteen.
